claims.text: Introducing a cooperative heterostructure with nano-coupled grains and nanoprecipitates into CoCrFeNi will lower its coefficient of friction from 25 °C to 800 °C.
Introducing the cooperative heterostructure will reduce the wear rate of CoCrFeNi from 25 °C to 800 °C.
The starting CoCrFeNi matrix has a homogeneous grain structure.
Controlled nanoprecipitation can produce nano-coupled grains and uniformly distributed nanoprecipitates in CoCrFeNi.
The intervention produces a cooperative heterostructure comprising nano-coupled grains and nanoprecipitates.
The nanoprecipitates reinforce the microstructure by pinning grain boundaries.
The nano-coupled heterostructure facilitates formation of a lubricious counter-oxide film during sliding.
The nano-coupled heterostructure facilitates retention of the lubricious counter-oxide film during sliding.
Grain-boundary pinning and retention of a lubricious oxide film mitigate friction at both low and high temperatures.
Grain-boundary pinning and retention of a lubricious oxide film mitigate wear at both low and high temperatures.
The modified alloy will have consistently lower friction than unmodified CoCrFeNi throughout the specified temperature range.
The modified alloy will have a lower wear rate than unmodified CoCrFeNi throughout the specified temperature range.
The proposed operating boundary is sliding from approximately 25 °C to 800 °C under high load in an oxidizing atmosphere.
The precise magnitude of friction and wear reduction is unknown pending experimental validation.
The long-term stability of the heterostructure under cyclic thermal stress is unknown pending experimental validation.
